core_obligations: Build the comparison cover (proof lines 1195-1208): let X_0, Y_0 be the sets of closed points; by the construction lemma there is an ind-Zariski A -> A' such that the component diagram of X' = Spec(A') over X is cartesian and the components of X' agree with those of Y; then X' is w-local and its closed points are the inverse image of X_0.

Produce the morphism to the cover (proof lines 1208-1214): Y and X' have the same space of connected components over X, so there is a continuous map Y -> X' over X; by the faithfulness statement for local isomorphisms this corresponds to a morphism of affine schemes Y -> X' over X.

Conclude (proof lines 1214-1219): since Y -> X maps Y_0 into X_0, the morphism Y -> X' maps Y_0 into X'_0, that is it is w-local; the isomorphism criterion for w-local morphisms of w-local schemes which are bijective on closed points then gives Y = X', so the composite A -> A' = B is ind-Zariski as required.
proof_roadmap: Construct an ind-Zariski cover of X with the same components as Y.
Use faithfulness for local isomorphisms to get a morphism Y to that cover.
Apply the isomorphism criterion for w-local morphisms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a ring map which identifies local rings and whose source and target spectra are w-local with a w-local morphism between them is ind-Zariski (statement lines 1184-1193). The proof (proof lines 1195-1221) constructs an ind-Zariski cover of X with the same components as Y, produces a morphism from Y to that cover by faithfulness for local isomorphisms, and concludes by the isomorphism criterion for w-local morphisms bijective on closed points. H2: a three-step comparison with three inputs, written out in full.
